issue_snapshot.title: `delete-full-slice` (FURB131) should not apply to `dict`s
issue_snapshot.body:
### Summary

[`delete-full-slice` (FURB131)](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/delete-full-slice/) should not apply to `dict`s, because slicing `dict`s raises an error, although the rule documentation says it works. The upstream Refurb rule only applies to `list`s. [Example](https://play.ruff.rs/6843ace6-2a9b-4e0e-b501-ac6b1216751c):
```console
$ cat >furb131.py <<'# EOF'
names = {"key": "value"}
del names[:]
# EOF

$ python furb131.py 2>&1 | tail -n 1
KeyError: slice(None, None, None)

$ refurb --enable FURB131 furb131.py; echo $?
0

$ ruff --isolated check --preview --select FURB131 furb131.py --unsafe-fixes --fix
Found 1 error (1 fixed, 0 remaining).

$ cat furb131.py
names = {"key": "value"}
names.clear()

$ python furb131.py; echo $?
0
```

### Version

ruff 0.16.0 (a2635fd8f 2026-07-23)

issue_snapshot.title: uv check --no-install-project
issue_snapshot.body:
### Summary

My project has extension modules that are heavy to build and require external non-Python dependencies. I do have *.pyi files for these extensions. I've setup `ty` such that I can install Python dependencies in .venv with `uv sync --no-install-project` and run `ty check` afterwards.

I would like to use `astral-sh/ty-pre-commit` hook, however I cannot figure out how to make it work without uv tying to install the project in  .venv. I'm guessing that `uv check` uses the `uv sync` machinery to setup/update .venv.

`uv check`  inherits most option related to extras/group installation from `uv sync`, but offers no control over the project installation. Therefore, IMHO it would make sense for `uv check` to accept a  `--no-install-project` flag just as `uv sync` does. 

### Example

```console
$ uv check --no-install-project ...
```

issue_snapshot.title: Reference pool mutex is taken on every attach which serializes multithreaded embedders
issue_snapshot.body:
`ReferencePool::drop_deferred_references` is called on every attach and it checks `is_empty` under a process global mutex.

For multithreaded embedders it becomes a serialization point. The mutex acquisition rate scales with threads and attach rate. Contended `std` mutex parks threads in the kernel.

I stumbled up on this while profiling the [Pants build system](https://github.com/pantsbuild/pants) engine (a Rust tokio runtime driving Python 3.14t code, pyo3 0.28.3) where I can measure anti-scaling behaviour attributed to `ReferencePool::drop_deferred_references` parking threads.

The proposed solution is to add an atomic bool to track whether the pool is "dirty". This is not a novel idea. #1608 introduced a dirty bool which was later removed. In #4174 it was noted that a dirty flag has the same cache-coherence traffic as the mutex's own futex word in the uncontended case. That does not hold under contention, though. 

#4174 also suggested replacing the mutex with a lock-free solution. The dirty flag is a more minimal fix and serves pants needs.

## Checklist

- [x] I have verified that that issue exists against the `master` branch of Django REST framework.
- [x] I have searched for similar issues in both open and closed tickets and cannot find a duplicate.
- [x] This is not a usage question. (Those should be directed to the [discussion group](https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/django-rest-framework) instead.)
- [x] This cannot be dealt with as a third party library. (We prefer new functionality to be [in the form of third party libraries](https://www.django-rest-framework.org/topics/third-party-resources/#about-third-party-packages) where possible.)
- [x] I have reduced the issue to the simplest possible case.
- [ ] I have included a failing test as a pull request. (If you are unable to do so we can still accept the issue.)

## Steps to reproduce

Using a DictField and custom partial update logic in a serializer, a condition such as:

`if not self.partial or "field-name" in data:`

Is always true when the request type is `multipart/form-data`, even if the field was not specified.  In fact, in this case, it seems like it is impossible to distinguish between an empty input and an unspecified input for that field.

## Expected behavior

The condition `if not self.partial or "field-name" in data` should only be true when the field was specified by the client, even when using `multipart/form-data` requests.

## Actual behavior

The condition is always true for `mutlipart/form-data` requests, even when the field was not specified as part of the request, and the update method has no way to distinguish between an empty input and an unspecified field.

Note that this is not the case for ListField, and the problem seems to be in the return of the function at https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/blob/master/rest_framework/utils/html.py#L69.  The equivalent function for a list field returns an empty value if no matching elements were found in the input.  For the dict field parsing logic, an empty dictionary is incorrectly returned.

issue_snapshot.title: websockets changed how it handles non-ASCII headers
issue_snapshot.body:
### Initial Checks

- [ ] I confirm this was discussed, and the maintainers suggest I open an issue.
- [x] I'm aware that if I created this issue without a discussion, it may be closed without a response.

_we didn't discuss this, but we collaborated before and I'm sure it's an actual issue_

### Description

In websockets 16.1 and in the upcoming 17.0, I changed how non-ASCII headers, which the HTTP spec disallows, are handled by websockets. This happened over two releases because I messed up and then cleaned up.

This will be backwards-incompatible for uvicorn; your tests will blow up next time you run them; and it has already blown up here: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16030 :-(

1. websockets 16.1 changed **receiving non-ASCII headers** from `.decode("ascii", errors="surrogateescape")` to `.decode("latin-1")` which never crashes, is fully reversible, and is what older versions of HTTP more or less tolerated; at least it's less esoteric than surrogate escapes. Currently, you're relying on the (undocumented) decoding algorithm to [undo it by re-encoding](https://github.com/Kludex/uvicorn/blob/7e11cc65f0642c823ef18ea01ff6b23af90aaa9e/uvicorn/protocols/websockets/websockets_sansio_impl.py#L196). This needs to be changed to `value.encode("latin-1"))`. Options for fixing:
  a. uvicorn switches to latin-1 to match websockets and requires websockets >=16.1
  b. uvicorn picks ascii + surrogate escapes or latin-1, conditional on the version of websockets — better if you don't want to constrain the version of websockets, but needs cleaning up later
  c. I release a 16.1.1 that undoes this change, and we solve it with a. or b. for websockets 17.0.

2. websockets 17.0 (not released yet) will change **sending non-ASCII headers** from `.encode()` to `.encode("latin-1")`. This ensures clean round-trips, accounting for the first change. Also this makes it possible to send anything that doesn't break HTTP, while previously only valid UTF-8 could be sent. Currently, you have a [test that sends a non-ASCII header](https://github.com/Kludex/uvicorn/blob/7e11cc65f0642c823ef18ea01ff6b23af90aaa9e/tests/protocols/test_websocket.py#L214). That will break. Options for fixing:
  a. add a `.encode().decode("latin-1")` somewhere in uvicorn to stick to UTF-8 and require websockets >= 17.0
  b. same as a., but conditional on the version of websockets 
  c. assert that the header is set to `bytes("abraão", "latin-1")` and require websockets >= 17.0; document the backwards incompatibility
  d. same as c., but conditional on the version of websockets 

I'm sorry I underestimated the backwards incompatibility :-(

This affects only the small subset of users how receive non-spec-compliant headers in the first place, so it's not major drama, but still worth fixing.

I'm happy to provide a PR for your favorite options.

```Text
0.51.0
```

issue_snapshot.title: Different rounding for timestamp and datetime when set last_modified
issue_snapshot.body:
Setting the `last_modified` property of `StreamResponse` rounds the value to seconds if it is `float` or `datetime`. But different rounding mode is used for `float` or `datetime`. If it is a `float` (timestamp), it is rounded toward +infinity. If it is an instance of `datetime`, it is rounded toward -infinity.

For example:
```
$ cat test_last_modified.py
from aiohttp.web import StreamResponse
from datetime import datetime, timezone

resp = StreamResponse()
dt = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
resp.last_modified = dt
print(resp.last_modified)
print(repr(resp.last_modified))
print(resp.headers["Last-Modified"])
resp.last_modified = dt.timestamp()
print(resp.last_modified)
print(repr(resp.last_modified))
print(resp.headers["Last-Modified"])
```
```
$ python test_last_modified.py
2020-12-02 09:51:02+00:00
datetime.datetime(2020, 12, 2, 9, 51, 2, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
Wed, 02 Dec 2020 09:51:02 GMT
2020-12-02 09:51:03+00:00
datetime.datetime(2020, 12, 2, 9, 51, 3, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
Wed, 02 Dec 2020 09:51:03 GMT
```
I don't know what direction is correct, but it should be the same.

issue_snapshot.title: Botocore mistakenly expects a reason phrase in "100 Continue" responses
issue_snapshot.body:
### Describe the bug

When making HTTP requests, botocore sends a 100-continue request to the server, expecting a `HTTP/1.1 100 Continue` response.

### Regression Issue

- [ ] Select this option if this issue appears to be a regression.

### Expected Behavior

The reason phrase is optional, so a `HTTP/1.1 100` response from the server is the correct behaviour.
Botocore should accept a `HTTP/1.1 100` response as correct.

### Current Behavior

If Botocore receives a `HTTP/1.1 100`, it interprets the response as not correct, and does not continue with the original request.

### Reproduction Steps

Start a service (locally) that sends `HTTP/1.1 100` responses to 100-continue requests, e.g. S3Mock:

```
docker run -e initialBuckets=my-bucket --rm -it -p 9090:9090 adobe/s3mock:4.0.0
```

Execute a `PutObject` request with a random file, e.g. the `README.rst` from the root of this repository, e.g. through `aws-cli` which uses boto3/botocore internally:

```
aws s3api put-object \
    --bucket x \
    --key y.txt \
    --content-type text/plain \
    --endpoint http://localhost:9090 \
    --body README.rst \
    --debug
```

The request will fail, as the Tomcat server used in S3Mock sends a `HTTP/1.1 100` as a response to the 100-continue request from botocore.

Example output:
```
2025-04-10 01:41:22,320 - MainThread - botocore.hooks - DEBUG - Event request-created.s3.PutObject: calling handler <bound method UserAgentString.rebuild_and_replace_user_agent_handler of <botocore.useragent.UserAgentString object at 0x1052779b0>>
2025-04-10 01:41:22,320 - MainThread - botocore.endpoint - DEBUG - Sending http request: <AWSPreparedRequest stream_output=False, method=PUT, url=http://localhost:9090/x/y.txt, headers={'Content-Type': b'text/plain', 'x-amz-sdk-checksum-algorithm': b'CRC32', 'User-Agent': b'aws-cli/2.25.13 md/awscrt#0.25.4 ua/2.1 os/macos#24.4.0 md/arch#arm64 lang/python#3.12.10 md/pyimpl#CPython m/N cfg/retry-mode#standard md/installer#source md/prompt#off md/command#s3api.put-object', 'Expect': b'100-continue', 'x-amz-checksum-crc32': b'NGSOug==', 'X-Amz-Date': b'20250409T234122Z', 'X-Amz-Content-SHA256': b'65dbc69741c062892a2842cc5d6099bbf02eefd4628d352d446c6c37cb0967da', 'Authorization': b'AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 Credential=NONE/20250409/us-east-1/s3/aws4_request, SignedHeaders=content-type;host;x-amz-checksum-crc32;x-amz-content-sha256;x-amz-date;x-amz-sdk-checksum-algorithm, Signature=e6a74e4aafab3b1c03e282cf2064d65dbb22af4396cb34460f69439d180f36d3', 'Content-Length': '42443'}>
2025-04-10 01:41:22,320 - MainThread - urllib3.connectionpool - DEBUG - Starting new HTTP connection (1): localhost:9090
2025-04-10 01:41:22,321 - MainThread - botocore.awsrequest - DEBUG - Waiting for 100 Continue response.
2025-04-10 01:41:22,324 - MainThread - botocore.hooks - DEBUG - Event needs-retry.s3.PutObject: calling handler <function _update_status_code at 0x101d1c2c0>
2025-04-10 01:41:22,324 - MainThread - botocore.hooks - DEBUG - Event needs-retry.s3.PutObject: calling handler <bound method RetryHandler.needs_retry of <botocore.retries.standard.RetryHandler object at 0x105277c80>>
2025-04-10 01:41:22,324 - MainThread - botocore.retries.standard - DEBUG - Retry needed, retrying request after delay of: 0.2322557477907542
```

### Possible Solution

In `botocore/awsrequest.py`, check for only 2 parts in the response instead of 3 since the reason phrase is optional.
This will let a `HTTP/1.1 100` response be detected correctly.

```
    def _is_100_continue_status(self, maybe_status_line):
        parts = maybe_status_line.split(None, 2)

        # Check for HTTP/<version> 100 (Continue)\r\n
        return (
            len(parts) >= 2
            and parts[0].startswith(b'HTTP/')
            and parts[1] == b'100'
        )
```

[S3Mock](https://github.com/adobe/S3Mock) is a library/service to locally test applications that integrate with AWS S3.

aws-cli version:
```
❯ aws --version
aws-cli/2.22.16 Python/3.12.8 Darwin/24.4.0 source/arm64
```

Reason phrase is optional, see https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-15.1

1.37.36

macOS, 15.4.1, 24E263

that PR introduced `_is_ambiguous` handling but did not address the spring-forward gap) #### Possible Duplicates - None ## Environment & Settings **Celery version**: main (post-5.4) **Relevant config**: ```python CELERY_TIMEZONE = "US/Eastern" # or any DST-observing zone CELERY_ENABLE_UTC = True ``` # Steps to Reproduce ## Required Dependencies - **Minimal Python Version**: 3.9 - **Minimal Celery Version**: 5.3 (after pytz deprecation / ZoneInfo migration) - **Minimal Kombu Version**: N/A - **Minimal Broker Version**: N/A - **Minimal Result Backend Version**: N/A - **Minimal OS and/or Kernel Version**: Any - **Minimal Broker Client Version**: N/A - **Minimal Result Backend Client Version**: N/A ### Python Packages
pip freeze Output:

celery @ git+https://github.com/celery/celery@main python-dateutil>=2.8

## Minimally Reproducible Test Case

```python from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo from datetime import datetime from dateutil import tz as dateutil_tz from celery.utils.time import make_aware tz = ZoneInfo("US/Eastern") # March 10, 2024: clocks spring forward at 2:00 AM -> 3:00 AM # 2:30 AM does not exist in US/Eastern on this date non_existent_dt = datetime(2024, 3, 10, 2, 30, 0) # Confirm it truly doesn't exist assert not dateutil_tz.datetime_exists(non_existent_dt.replace(tzinfo=tz)), \ "Expected non-existent time in spring-forward gap" result = make_aware(non_existent_dt, tz) # The UTC offset will be -05:00 (EST) instead of the correct post-transition -04:00 (EDT) # The function returns silently with no warning or error print(result) print(result.utcoffset()) # prints -1 day, 19:00:00 (i.e. -05:00, which is wrong) # To see the beat scheduler impact: from celery.schedules import crontab schedule = crontab(hour=2, minute=30, app=None) # On the spring-forward night, remaining_delta produces a next-run datetime # landing in the gap, which make_aware() resolves incorrectly, # causing the task to either be skipped or fire an hour late. ```

# Expected Behavior `make_aware()` should detect when a naive datetime falls inside a spring-forward DST gap (a time that does not exist in the given timezone) and advance the datetime to the first valid moment after the gap — consistent with how most DST-aware frameworks (Django, Arrow, pendulum) handle this case. `dateutil_tz.datetime_exists()` is already available via the existing `from dateutil import tz as dateutil_tz` import in `celery/utils/time.py` and can be used directly. Proposed fix in `celery/utils/time.py`: ```python def make_aware(dt: datetime, tz: tzinfo) -> datetime: """Set timezone for a :class:`~datetime.datetime` object.""" dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=tz) if _is_ambiguous(dt, tz): # Fall-back: two wall-clock instants map to the same local time. # Pick the earlier UTC instant (fold=0, DST still active). dt = min(dt.replace(fold=0), dt.replace(fold=1)) elif _can_detect_ambiguous(tz) and not dateutil_tz.datetime_exists(dt): # Spring-forward gap: this local time does not exist. # Advance to the post-transition instant (fold=1). dt = dt.replace(fold=1) return dt ``` A corresponding `_is_nonexistent()` helper (mirroring `_is_ambiguous()`) could also be added for clarity and testability. # Actual Behavior `make_aware()` only guards against ambiguous (fall-back) times via `_is_ambiguous()`. There is no equivalent check for non-existent (spring-forward) times. When a crontab's computed next-run datetime lands inside the spring-forward gap: 1. `make_aware()` calls `dt.replace(tzinfo=tz)` on the non-existent time with no further correction. 2. The resulting datetime carries the pre-transition UTC offset (e.g. `-05:00` EST instead of `-04:00` EDT). 3. `remaining_estimate()` therefore computes a next-run time that is **one hour later than intended** in UTC. 4. On the affected night the task either **fires one hour late** or is **silently skipped** entirely, with no log warning or exception raised. This is the exact spring-forward counterpart to #10107 (fall-back skipping), but currently has no handling in the codebase. I WOULD LIKE TO WORK ON THIS ISSUE AND GET IT FIXED AS SOON AS POSSIBLE. PLEASE ASSIGN IT TO ME.

issue_snapshot.title: Better heuristic for when to optimize `target()` metrics
issue_snapshot.body:
Currently, we run all of our optimizer routines [exactly once, starting at (or just after) half of our `max_examples` budget](https://github.com/HypothesisWorks/hypothesis/blob/9fce400120bcb7fcdf66626a5c6525f84db21e59/hypothesis-python/src/hypothesis/internal/conjecture/engine.py#L738-L743).  This works pretty well for the default `max_examples=100`, but I've noticed increasing use of Hypothesis with very large example budgets (and `target()`) for one-off searches for some example - and we can do much better for this workflow.  Specifically, we should:

- better support interleaving of ordinary generation with targeted optimization; e.g. "run an optimize step, then generate that many examples, then the next optimize step...".  This still aims to spend up-to-half our total examples optimizing.
- pick a smoother heuristic for when-to-optimize.  Initial proposal: maintain current behaviour for `max_examples < 1000`; for `max_examples >= 1000` use the incremental mixture instead, starting after 200 examples generated by our usual means.
- for long runs, we might finish running the optimizer.  How should we decide to start a second full pass?  We don't want unproductive re-runs (as may be implicated in #2985), but an additional run must *sometimes* make sense...

issue_snapshot.title: WSGIRequestHandler sends 100 Continue twice when client sends Expect: 100-continue
issue_snapshot.body:
`WSGIRequestHandler` sends `HTTP/1.1 100 Continue` twice when a client includes the `Expect: 100-continue` header. Python's `BaseHTTPRequestHandler.parse_request()` calls `handle_expect_100()` which sends the first response. Then `run_wsgi()` ([serving.py L313-314](https://github.com/pallets/werkzeug/blob/main/src/werkzeug/serving.py#L313-L314)) independently checks the same header and writes a second one. Neither layer clears the header after acting on it.

HTTP clients that strictly parse interim responses — notably the AWS SDK's Netty-based async client — treat the second `100 Continue` as the start of the final response, causing all uploads to fail with status code 100.

```python
import socket
import threading
from werkzeug.serving import make_server


def app(environ, start_response):
    # Read and discard request body
    environ["wsgi.input"].read()
    start_response("200 OK", [("Content-Type", "text/plain")])
    return [b"ok"]


server = make_server("127.0.0.1", 9876, app, threaded=True)
thread = threading.Thread(target=server.handle_request)
thread.start()

sock = socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", 9876))
sock.sendall(
    b"PUT /test HTTP/1.1\r\n"
    b"Host: 127.0.0.1:9876\r\n"
    b"Content-Length: 5\r\n"
    b"Expect: 100-continue\r\n"
    b"\r\n"
)

# Collect the full response before sending the body
import time
time.sleep(0.5)
response = sock.recv(4096)
print(response.decode())

sock.sendall(b"hello")
time.sleep(0.5)
response = sock.recv(4096)
print(response.decode())

sock.close()
thread.join()
server.server_close()

```

**Expected:** One `HTTP/1.1 100 Continue` response, followed by the final `200 OK` after the body is sent.

**Actual:** Two `HTTP/1.1 100 Continue` responses are sent before the final `200 OK`. Raw output:

```
HTTP/1.1 100 Continue

HTTP/1.1 100 Continue

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
...
```

A minimal fix would be to override `handle_expect_100` to suppress the stdlib's response, since `run_wsgi()` already handles it:

```python
def handle_expect_100(self) -> bool:
    return True
```

Environment:

- Python version: 3.12
- Werkzeug version: 3.1.7 (main branch)
